title: Prooven Platform
subtitle: Last-Mile Delivery Verification & Billing Platform
shortDescription: Last-mile delivery verification and billing platform for ABC Express distribution programs — offline-first courier PWA, POD evidence, BAST-to-billing pipeline, and an AI operations agent over a Rust graph/simulation core.
longDescription: Prooven is the last-mile operations platform used by ABC Express to run government and enterprise distribution programs — IFP, Pusbuk, Kemensos — delivering tens of thousands of shipments to schools and institutions across Indonesia. It closes the loop between the upstream Antero logistics system and physical delivery: couriers scan TTK waybills in an offline-first PWA, capture proof-of-delivery photos and serial-number verification, and backoffice staff process BAST handover documents into billing — all over a Supabase/PostgreSQL data layer with row-level security, a Go edge gateway, a Rust knowledge-graph + Monte Carlo engine, and a DeepAgents.js AI agent for operational decision support.
problem: Last-mile delivery for large distribution programs was hard to verify end-to-end: proof of delivery lived on paper, BAST documents drove billing manually, field couriers worked in low-connectivity regions, and clients had no trustworthy read-only view into delivery progress.
solution: A centralized verification platform spanning field capture to finance: an offline-first courier PWA that survives dead zones, a backoffice dashboard for SLA monitoring, BAST processing, and billing (Pra-PI → PI → SI → Lunas), client-facing view-only access scoped by RLS, and an external JSON:API for program stakeholders — plus a Rust simulation/graph layer and AI agent for forecasting and analysis.

decisions.title: Offline-first over always-online
decisions.rationale: Couriers deliver to remote kecamatan with unstable connectivity — the PWA treats the network as optional, queueing forms and compressed photos in IndexedDB and syncing on recovery.

decisions.title: Postgres as the enforcement layer
decisions.rationale: Client scoping, role guards (is_client(), client_project_keys()), and project isolation live in RLS policies and security-definer RPCs — not just in the API — so external viewers and internal roles share one enforced model.

decisions.title: Polyglot by workload, not by fashion
decisions.rationale: Rust owns graph/simulation compute, Go owns the edge (auth, rate limiting, proxying), TypeScript owns UI and agent logic — connected through explicit gRPC contracts.

decisions.title: AI advises, workflows decide
decisions.rationale: The agent forecasts routes, queries shipments, and answers operational questions — mutations still flow through auditable RPC and edge-function paths.

decisions.title: Scale engineered ahead of volume
decisions.rationale: Trigram indexes, keyset pagination, thumbnail media pipeline, realtime bulk-op guards, and append-only retention were designed against a measured 80K-shipment / ~1 TB media capacity model, not guessed.

impact: Runs last-mile POD verification for ABC Express distribution programs — ~37–48K shipments in the IFP 2025 cycle, engineered for ±80K shipments and ~640K media objects in the 2026 program
Turns paper proof-of-delivery into a verifiable digital chain — scan → serial verify → photo evidence → BAST → invoice
Gives external program clients a live, scoped view of their own deliveries
Brings graph reasoning and Monte Carlo forecasting into real routing and SLA decisions
